subtitle: In a besieged kingdom, a painter turns survival into color

panels.shot: epic three-quarter view, painter in foreground, fortress-city of Udaipur and distant Aravalli hills behind
panels.action: Sahibdin stands holding a vivid manuscript folio, his figure half-lit by a lamp, while behind him the terraces of Udaipur and the rugged Aravalli hills rise under a stormy sky, hinting at war and courtly splendor.

dialogue.text: As Mewar bled and rebuilt between Mughal steel and Rajput stubbornness, Sahibdin and his fellows turned fragile paper into a second battlefield of memory.

i18n.hi: जब मेवाड़ मुग़ल तलवार और राजपूत जिद के बीच लहूलुहान होकर फिर खड़ा हो रहा था, साहिबदीन और उसके साथी नाज़ुक कागज़ को यादों का दूसरा रण बना रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide overhead view of hill fortress town
panels.action: High in the Aravalli hills, the small hill capital of Chawand clings to the slopes, stone walls and houses huddled together as mist curls around the ridges.

dialogue.text: In 1605, while emperors measured India in forts and revenues, a small hill town named Chawand quietly dated a different conquest in the colophon of a painted songbook.

i18n.hi: १६०५ में, जब बादशाह भारत को किलों और लगान में तौल रहे थे, पहाड़ों में एक छोटा शहर चावंड चुपचाप एक रंगी हुई गीत-पुस्तक के आख़िरी लेख में दूसरी ही फतह दर्ज कर रहा था।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot of scribe at low desk
panels.action: Inside a modest but busy atelier room in Chawand, a scribe bends over a palm-leaf-like paper, his reed pen poised as he inscribes a neat Sanskrit colophon under a painted page.

dialogue.text: That colophon, in a Ragamala painted for Maharana Pratap’s hill court, anchored the Mewar school in time and place: Chawand, 1605, music and devotion set in bold, flat color.

i18n.hi: उस आख़िरी लेख ने, महाराणा प्रताप की पहाड़ी दरबार के लिए बनी रागमाला में, मेवाड़ की चित्रशाला को समय और जगह में गाड़ दिया: चावंड, १६०५, संगीत और भक्ति को मोटे, सपाट रंगों में जड़ दिया गया।

panels.shot: close-up on a Ragamala folio lying on a low desk
panels.action: A single Ragamala folio lies on a rough wooden plank, showing a stylized pavilion, a noble listener and a musician under a dark sky, with wide staring eyes and fields of solid, unshaded color.

dialogue.text: Its anonymous painters kept faith with the hard lines and jewel-box colors of older Western Indian and Jain manuscripts, even as Mughal ateliers down on the plains chased softness and shadow.

i18n.hi: इसके गुमनाम चित्रकारों ने पुराने पश्चिमी भारतीय और जैन पांडुलिपियों की कड़ी रेखाओं और गहना-से रंगों से नाता नहीं तोड़ा, जबकि नीचे मैदानों में मुग़ल कारखाने नरमी और साये के पीछे दौड़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Chawand court hall, with painters at edge
panels.action: In a simple audience hall at Chawand, Rajput nobles stand armed near Maharana Pratap, while at the dimmer edge two artisans kneel over a low desk, carefully lifting bright folios in their stained fingers.

dialogue.text: Mewar’s hill court had little gold and fewer comforts, but it gave shelter to painters and scribes; in those cramped rooms, color became a way of saying, ‘We are still here.’

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ की पहाड़ी दरबार के पास न सोना ज़्यादा था, न सुख-सुविधा; पर उसने चित्रकारों और लेखकों को आसरा दिया, उन तंग कमरों में रंग ही एक पुकार बन गए—‘हम अब भी हैं।’

panels.shot: transitional montage-like mid-shot, younger Sahibdin among other apprentices
panels.action: Years later in Udaipur, a young Sahibdin sits cross-legged among fellow apprentices in a brighter atelier, copying a fragment of an older Chawand-style painting pinned beside his fresh, more detailed sheet.

dialogue.text: By the time Udaipur rose from the valleys and Shah Jahan sat on the Peacock Throne, a named hand appears in the record: Sahibdin, one among many in a restless court workshop.

i18n.hi: जब तक घाटियों से उदयपुर उठ चुका था और शाहजहाँ मयूर सिंहासन पर बैठ चुका था, रजिस्टरों में एक नाम उभरता है: साहिबदीन, बेचैन दरबारी कारखाने की भीड़ में एक हस्ती।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Sahibdin toward his work
panels.action: From behind Sahibdin’s shoulder, we see him carefully drawing sharp, angular figures with large eyes, then pausing to glance at a delicate Mughal manuscript open nearby, its shaded faces and receding landscape a contrast to his page.

dialogue.text: Rajput patrons owned Mughal albums and princes travelled to imperial camps; in the Mewar atelier, flat crimson backgrounds met new ideas of space, profile and portrait brought from Agra and beyond.

i18n.hi: राजपूत सरदारों के पास मुग़ल मलफ़ोज़ात थे, राजकुमार शाही छावनियों तक जाते थे; मेवाड़ की कार्यशाला में सपाट सुर्ख पृष्ठभूमि अब आगरा और दूर-दूर से आई नई जगह, प्रोफाइल और पोर्ट्रेट की सोच से टकरा रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, court official visiting atelier
panels.action: A court officer in fine cloth steps into the atelier, examining a folio while Sahibdin rises respectfully, holding another unfinished sheet that shows a deity standing under a stylized arch and a distant palace rendered with increased depth.

dialogue.speaker: court officer
dialogue.text: The Maharana desires a great Ramayana. The gods will ride your colors, Sahibdin.

i18n.hi: महाराणा एक महान रामायण चाहते हैं। देवता तेरे रंगों पर सवार होंगे, साहिबदीन।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Sahibdin looking up, brush in hand
panels.action: Sahibdin looks up from his pigments, his face lit by the warm glow of a lamp, brush held in mid-air as if weighing the enormity of the Ramayana commission.

dialogue.text: Between about 1649 and 1652, colophons begin to speak his name, tying Sahibdin to vast illustrated Ramayana manuscripts that would demand not just skill, but a vision of what Mewar wished to remember.

i18n.hi: लगभग १६४९ से १६५२ के बीच, आख़िरी लेख उसका नाम बोलने लगते हैं, साहिबदीन को उन विराट चित्रित रामायणों से जोड़ते हुए, जिन्हें हुनर के साथ-साथ यह कल्पना भी चाहिए थी कि मेवाड़ क्या याद रखना चाहता है।

panels.shot: busy wide interior of Udaipur atelier, multiple artists working
panels.action: In a large Udaipur workshop, several painters sit in rows, one outlining figures, another applying flat base colors, others adding patterns and details, while Sahibdin moves among them, correcting and demonstrating on a folio of Rama in battle.

dialogue.text: These were not solitary labors; the Ramayana and later Bhagavata Purana were products of a collaborative atelier, with Sahibdin’s hand and eye guiding many sheets, but countless anonymous brushes sharing the load.

i18n.hi: ये किसी एक की साधना नहीं थीं; रामायण और बाद की भागवतपुराण एक सामूहिक कारखाने की देन थीं, जहाँ साहिबदीन की नज़र और हाथ कई पन्नों को दिशा दे रहे थे, पर अनगिनत गुमनाम कूचियाँ भी मेहनत बाँट रही थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a Ramayana battle folio under Sahibdin’s hand
panels.action: A close view shows Sahibdin painting a Ramayana battle scene: Rama’s chariot presses forward, demons tumble in stylized poses, the sky a band of burning orange, the ground broken into patterned registers, no shadows but a sense of ordered chaos.

dialogue.text: Unlike Mughal chronicles that shadowed every fold, these pages held to flat planes and rhythmic pattern; yet through crowded fields and tilted ground, Sahibdin conjured movement, noise, and the press of war.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल इतिहासों की तरह हर मोड़ पर साया नहीं, ये पन्ने सपाट सतहों और लयदार बुनावट पर टिके रहे; फिर भी भरे हुए मैदानों और झुके हुए ज़मीनों के बीच साहिबदीन ने हलचल, शोर और जंग की ठसाठस भीड़ जगा दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sahibdin mixing pigments, jars around him
panels.action: Sahibdin squats amidst small ceramic cups, grinding mineral pigments on a stone slab, fingers stained blue and red, as he tests a streak of deep indigo against the white margin of a page.

dialogue.text: His palette drew from older Jain traditions—hot reds, cool greens, gleaming yellows—yet new, subtler tones crept in, hints of sky gradation or modeled faces, absorbed from imperial art but bent to Mewar stories.

i18n.hi: उसकी रंग-पट्टी पुराने जैन रंगों से भरी थी—तेज़ लाल, ठंडी हरी, चमकती पीली—फिर भी नए, हल्के शेड धीरे-धीरे घुस आए, आसमान की हल्की ढलान या चेहरे की गढ़न के इशारे, जो शाही कला से सीखे गए, पर मेवाड़ की कहानियों में ढल गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Udaipur City Palace terrace, night, with atelier lit
panels.action: At night, the terraces of Udaipur City Palace rise above the dark lake; one upper window glows bright, where the atelier continues to work, Sahibdin’s silhouette visible against rows of drying folios pinned to cords.

dialogue.text: Outside, Shah Jahan’s campaigns pushed and pulled Rajput loyalties; inside these lit rooms, stories of Rama and Krishna gave Mewar a parallel script, where its rulers could imagine their place among the righteous.

i18n.hi: बाहर शाहजहाँ की मुहिमें राजपूत वफ़ादारियों को खींच-तान रही थीं; इन रोशन कमरों के भीतर राम और कृष्ण की कथाएँ मेवाड़ को एक दूसरा लेख देती थीं, जहाँ उसके राजे खुद को धर्मयुद्ध में अपना स्थान सोच सकते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sahibdin painting a courtly scene rather than myth
panels.action: Sahibdin bends over a folio showing a Mewar ruler in audience, attendants in precise profile, a Mughal-style tented canopy behind, but the ground slopes upward in the old Mewar manner, compressing space.

dialogue.text: Other works from the same decades show courtly life: processions, durbars, hunts. Here too, his workshop balanced imperial naturalism with the stubborn geometry of Rajput taste, stitching a local identity into borrowed forms.

i18n.hi: उसी दौर की दूसरी रचनाएँ दरबारी ज़िंदगी दिखाती हैं: जुलूस, दरबार, शिकार। यहाँ भी उसकी कार्यशाला ने शाही नैसर्गिकता को राजपूती ज़िद्दी ज्यामिति के साथ तौला, उधार ली हुई शकलों में अपना लोक-चिह्न टाँक दिया।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot, Sahibdin and a younger apprentice
panels.action: In a quieter moment, Sahibdin gestures toward an older Chawand Ragamala page laid beside a fresh folio, explaining something to a younger apprentice who listens intently, brush resting over his knee.

dialogue.speaker: sahibdin
dialogue.text: Remember their lines, but hear our time. Let the old song carry a new voice.

i18n.hi: उनकी रेखाएँ याद रखो, पर हमारी घड़ी सुनो। पुराना गीत गाए, पर आवाज़ नई हो।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of scattered folios in a modern archive
panels.action: In a modern archival setting, gloved hands arrange dispersed folios of the Ramayana and Bhagavata Purana on a table, their edges not matching, each labeled from different museums and collections.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, these manuscripts lie scattered across museums and libraries, their sequences broken; yet colophons and style allow scholars to trace the web of hands and patrons tying them back to Udaipur.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतते-बीतते ये पांडुलिपियाँ संग्रहालयों और किताबघरों में इधर-उधर बिखर गईं, उनकी कड़ियाँ टूट गईं; पर आख़िरी लेख और शैली आज भी विद्वानों को हाथों और सरपरस्तों का जाल पकड़ने देते हैं, जो इन्हें फिर से उदयपुर से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: close-up of a digitized folio on a computer screen
panels.action: A digitized high-resolution image of a Sahibdin-attributed folio glows on a computer monitor, zoomed into the minute patterns on a garment, while a cursor hovers, revealing every line and brushstroke.

dialogue.text: Recent digitization has brought these pages back into a single virtual space, letting eyes far from Mewar watch how a seventeenth-century workshop layered myth, memory and politics onto paper.

i18n.hi: नई डिजिटली नकल ने इन पन्नों को फिर एक आभासी जगह में जोड़ दिया है, जिससे मेवाड़ से दूर बैठी आँखें देख सकें कि सत्रहवीं सदी की एक कार्यशाला ने कैसे मिथक, याद और सियासत को परत-दर-परत कागज़ पर रखा।

panels.shot: poetic closing shot, older Sahibdin silhouetted against sunrise over hills
panels.action: An older Sahibdin sits on a palace parapet at dawn, a closed manuscript resting on his lap as the sun rises over the Aravalli hills, turning the lake and city below into bands of gold and shadow.

dialogue.text: Mewar’s battles left scars in stone; its painters, from the unnamed hands of Chawand to Sahibdin’s marked folios, left a different record, proving a civilization by what it keeps creating when survival itself is in doubt.

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ की लड़ाइयों ने पत्थर पर निशान छोड़े; उसके चित्रकारों ने, चावंड के बेनाम हाथों से लेकर साहिबदीन के लिखित पन्नों तक, दूसरी तरह का दस्तावेज़ छोड़ा, यह साबित करते हुए कि कोई सभ्यता वही है जो वह बनाती रहती है, जब जीना ही दाँव पर हो।

title_i18n.en: Sahibdin Paints the Colors of Mewar
title_i18n.hi: साहिबदीन ने मेवाड़ को रंगों में रचा

subtitle_i18n.en: In a besieged kingdom, a painter turns survival into color
subtitle_i18n.hi: घिरे हुए राज्य में, एक चित्रकार ने जीना रंगों में बदल दिया
